definition: Covered with scurf: thin, flaking, scale-like matter shed from a surface, especially the dry outer bark of trees or the skin of plants as they harden into dormancy.
etymology: From Old English sceorf, related to Old Norse skurfur and Middle Low German schorf, all rooted in a Germanic base meaning to cut or scrape. The word carries the memory of a knife drawn lightly across bark, lifting pale curls of dead surface away.
usage: October trees often go scurfed before they go bare, their trunks pale and flaking in the thin afternoon light, as though the season itself were peeling off an old skin to show the grey beneath.
